questions.q: Which of these is a model family available through Azure OpenAI Service?
options: GPT-4o and the o-series reasoning models
Only a single fixed chat model with no alternatives
Models exclusive to Azure that OpenAI itself doesn't offer
Only image generation, no text or chat models
questions.explain: Azure OpenAI Service offers the same OpenAI model families available directly from OpenAI, including GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, and the o-series reasoning models, plus embeddings, images, and audio models.

questions.q: How is an Azure OpenAI resource created?
options: Only through a separate OpenAI.com account, unrelated to Azure
The same way as any other Azure resource — through Create a resource in the Azure portal
It is created automatically the first time you sign up for Azure
It requires a phone call to Microsoft support
questions.explain: Azure OpenAI is a standard Azure resource, created through Create a resource in the Azure portal just like a storage account or VM.

questions.q: What pricing tier is currently available for Azure OpenAI resources?
options: Basic, Standard, and Premium
Free tier only
Standard S0 — currently the only tier offered
A custom tier you negotiate per resource
questions.explain: As of this course, Standard S0 is the only pricing tier available when creating an Azure OpenAI resource.

questions.q: In Azure OpenAI, what value do you pass as the "model" parameter in an API request?
options: Your deployment name, which you chose when you deployed the model
A randomly generated GUID
The exact same model name string OpenAI's own API uses, always
Your Azure subscription ID
questions.explain: Azure OpenAI routes by deployment name, not the underlying model name. The deployment name is chosen by you at deploy time and can differ from the model it points to.

questions.q: What is the practical benefit of Azure OpenAI's deployment-name routing?
options: It makes the API slower but more secure
You can swap the underlying model behind a deployment name without changing application code
It removes the need for an API key
It guarantees the model never needs updating
questions.explain: Because application code calls a deployment name rather than a model name directly, you can upgrade the underlying model (e.g., GPT-4o to GPT-4.1) without touching the calling code, as long as the deployment name stays the same.
